source.stem: Which statement about bonding is not correct?

options.text: Carbon can form four single covalent bonds.
Chlorine atoms react to gain a noble gas electronic structure.
Covalent bonding involves losing and gaining electrons.
Hydrogen molecules have the formula H₂.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The property that allows copper to be drawn into wires is malleability.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Steel is unsuitable for making wires because it contains carbon.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Shiny coal is suitable for drawing into wires.

intelligence.enrichment: Ductility is the property by which materials can be drawn into wires, and it is mainly possessed by metals. Copper, aluminium, and steel can be used as wires, while coal and sulfur are not ductile. The ability to be drawn into wire determines whether the material is suitable for wire-based uses. The learner correctly applies this rule: Ductility is the property by which materials can be drawn into wires, and it is mainly possessed by metals. Copper, aluminium, and steel can be used as wires, while coal and sulfur are not ductile. Any strong or hard solid can be made into wire if enough force is used.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: The world of metals and non-metals. The student must decide: When a material must be drawn into wire, decide whether ductility makes a metal such as copper, aluminium, or steel suitable and coal or sulfur unsuitable. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key.
